title: He wasn’t supposed to hear God.
paragraphs: He wasn’t supposed to hear God.

Not like that.
Not that clearly.
Not in a season when heaven had gone silent.
a boy was lying in the dark—closer than everyone else.
And somewhere between sleep and surrender…
But here’s the tension nobody talks about:

Why was the voice of God rare…
when the temple was full?

Why was heaven quiet…
when religion was loud?
Why did a child hear what priests ignored?
Because this is not just Samuel’s story.

We have Bibles on our shelves… but silence in our spirits.
We have sermons in our ears… but distance in our hearts.
We have worship playlists… but no trembling when God speaks.
And deep down, you know it.
Because you can be around holy things…
and still be far from God.
Living in open sin—inside sacred space (1 Samuel 2:12–17).
Didn’t carry the weight of God’s holiness with urgency.
This is where it gets uncomfortable.
Because Eli is not just a character.
You know that habit you’ve been excusing?

That thing you keep near…
while still trying to stay “close to God”?

“Now the word of the Lord was rare in those days; there was no frequent vision.”
—1 Samuel 3:1
Because persistent, unrepented sin dulls spiritual hearing.

“Samuel was lying down in the temple of the Lord, where the ark of God was.”
—1 Samuel 3:3
While others got used to the silence…
he positioned himself for a whisper.
But Samuel didn’t recognize the voice.
“Here I am, for you called me.”
You can be close to God…
and still be learning His voice.
God did not reject Samuel for confusion.
Because some of you are in that place right now.
trying to separate your thoughts from His voice.
And you’re afraid of getting it wrong.
God is not playing hide and seek with your calling.

“Speak, Lord, for Your servant hears.”
—1 Samuel 3:10
This is where the emotional trigger hits:
Because the presence of God is not just comforting—
We love a God who whispers peace…
but we resist a God who exposes sin.
And here is where the story explodes into the Gospel.
Samuel could lie near the ark…
but he could never enter the fullness of God’s presence.
Still distance between holy God and sinful man.
another voice would break the silence.

“In the beginning was the Word… and the Word was God…
And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us.”
—John 1:1,14
And this is the truth we cannot soften:

“Your iniquities have made a separation between you and your God.”
—Isaiah 59:2
But God did not leave it there.

“And behold, the curtain of the temple was torn in two, from top to bottom.”
—Matthew 27:51
But because Jesus became sin for us.

“For our sake He made Him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.”
—2 Corinthians 5:21
you don’t just sleep near the presence.
You become a dwelling place of God.

“Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you…?”
—1 Corinthians 6:19
The same God Samuel trembled before…
now lives in those who belong to Jesus.
So why are we still distant?
Why are we still pretending not to hear?
with what God is calling us to confront.
Return to the voice of God.
Stop negotiating with what nailed Jesus to the cross.
Even if it calls you out of something you’ve held onto for years.
Because His voice does not destroy—
His nearness is not meant to comfort your sin—
Jesus is not asking for perfection.
So don’t stay in the silence.
If this pierced your heart, don’t ignore it.
